cost.question: Plan #20 §10 Q4: settle release's UUIDs/day offline — reproduce the production `get_proto_small`/`get_proto_big` query shape, replay it over the full 329-pair set at the deployed cadence, measure the per-tick lifetime UNION factor properly, convert to $/month, and answer the ≤10 / ≥40 tripwire.
cost.answer: The instrument disagreement is CLOSED and the window disagreement is NOT. Replaying the exact production proto query over all 329 pairs gives **14.31 kept protos/pair** (median 20, 55.0% capped at 20) = **35.39 single-tick UUIDs/day** over 133 run-days — 1.56x the 61-day shape (22.69/day) and 8.9x the no-date/7-day shape (3.98/day), and 22% above the n=30 figure the plan quotes (11.7/pair). The lifetime union factor, measured properly (72 ticks/day × every one of a pair's mean 4.45 picked run-days, 5,621 live queries), is **1.35-1.47x population-weighted** — not the 1.2-2.2x guess, and it is exactly 1.000x on the 45% of pairs that never reach the cap (analytic: if card ≤ 20 every proto is kept at every tick). That puts release at **47.9-51.9 UUIDs/day at the long-run rate** ⇒ **$1,377-2,086/month**, i.e. the **≥40/day tripwire FIRES** — but that is 41-45% of nightly's 116.1 uuid rows/day and $1.4-2.1k against nightly's $3,339-4,476/month, so "a second nightly-sized bill" overstates it. The residual band is 7.1x wide and it is entirely the WINDOW: the same production instrument reads 4.97 single-tick UUIDs/day (⇒ 6.7-7.3 UUIDs/day, ≤10 fires) over the last 36 run-days and 35.39 over 133. Neither published projection was right: $207-740 describes only the quietest month, and $960-4,050 brackets the long-run answer but its top half is unreachable at any window I measured.

cost.decision_implication: Rewrite §10 Q4's tripwire row and delete the 9.4x band from §1.5 and §7.3. The plan should now say: the UUID rate has been settled OFFLINE and Phase 3 is not needed to buy it — production shape = 14.31 kept protos/pair over the full 329 (not 11.7 on 30), lifetime union factor = 1.35-1.47x (not 1.2-2.2x on n=4), so release is 47.9-51.9 UUIDs/day = $1,377-2,086/month at the long-run rate and 6.7-7.3/day = $194-293/month at the last-36-run-day rate. State the verdict as: the ≥40/day tripwire FIRES on the 4.3-month rate, so the $207-740 projection is refuted except in the quietest month; but "a second nightly-sized bill" should be struck and replaced with "41-45% of nightly's UUID rate and 31-47% of its bill", and the $2,100-4,050 top half of the other projection should be marked unreachable. Because §10 Q1 offered "≤10/day makes release arguable" and the answer is 48-52/day at the expected rate, Q1's recommendation (do not arm release triage) stands on cost as written — but the residual disagreement should be re-labelled a WINDOW/build-cadence question, not an instrument one, and it is a 7.1x spread that a single held cycle would sample only once and could easily sample from the quiet regime, which is a further argument against buying Phase 3 for this. Add to §13: a fixed-lower-bound `date` is not merely wrong, its error CHANGES SIGN with the age of the row it measures (the 61-day shape overstates by 17% on a recent 27-pair sample and understates by 36% over 133 run-days), and a shape with no as-of anchor at all cannot be replayed — the no-`date` query returns zero protos on 48% of the population when re-run later. Also record, so it is not rebuilt: the 72×/day cadence adds ZERO pairs to the selector (x1.00 on both a burst and a quiet day), the union factor is exactly 1.000 for the 45% of pairs that never reach the cap, `get_proto_small`'s 10,000 chunk facet never binds on release (worst chunk 845), and the plan's "0.75/day quiet steady state" is a switch-on artefact worth 0.42/day under continuous attribution.

product.question: Plan #20 §10 Q2: is the below-both-upstream-floors release-only crash population a real product, or is it already covered by existing triage? The deciding number: how many of the 37 have no open bug.
product.answer: It is a real, un-covered population, but it is roughly a third the size the plan claims and its exemplar list is half wrong. The deciding number came out strongly pro-product: 29 of the 37 (78.4%) have NO open same-application non-meta bug through the repo's own venue chain, 18 of 37 (48.6%) have no same-application bug at all in any status, and 0 of 37 carry a `topcrash*` keyword — against 26 of 37 (70.3%) on a control of the 37 loudest release signatures (Fisher p=2.6e-11). Neither the 97-bug 2026 `topcrash` population, nor `release-mgmt-account-bot` (whose own 60 signatures have a median of 2 release installs and 23 of 60 at zero), nor aryx's 109 is on any of them. But the supply is overstated: b1 forgot `utils.get_search_channel`, so 10/200 and 37/350 become 6/200 and 23/350 with `aurora` included, and re-measured in the gate's own unit (max upstream build-DAY report count, plus the from-zero branch `is_spike` does not floor-gate) the airtight "nightly and beta could never have selected it" set is 0 of the top 100, 6 of 200 (3.0%) and 24 of 350 (6.9%). Of the plan's five named "Firefox code" exemplars only two survive: `LdrLoadDll` is an OS-loader frame at bit_flip_rate 0.695, `GMPChild::RecvPreloadLibs` has 1,075 nightly reports on one build (the "1" was an install cardinality), and `MediaChangeMonitor::DecodeFirstSample` clears no floor but nightly's from-zero branch could have fired on its single report. RECOMMEND: ship the narrow signature-level alarm — ~140 HTTP calls, 2-4 minutes, zero model tokens — which over the last 90 days would have emitted 14.7 signatures/month raw, 77% un-bugged, 3.0/month that are un-bugged Firefox/Gecko code and hardware-clean.

(b) Called `bugzilla_apply._open_bugs_for_signature` -> `_split_by_application(bugs,"Firefox")` -> `_split_out_metas` directly, one signature at a time, unauthenticated. caveats: Release Socorro counts are throttled class-dependently 10%-100% (antenna MOZILLA_RULES), so every release install/report figure here is a lower bound on the real population by a factor between 1 and 10 — an interval, not a point. Nightly and beta are unthrottled, which is why the 'never selectable upstream' side is a census and the conclusion is not weakened.

`_cardinality.install_time` over 30 or 90 days is neither installations nor install-days — install_time resets on update, so it is a ceiling. I used it only for RANKING the release panel and, for the airtight bar, only through the exact direction `reports >= distinct installs on a given buildid`.

P_strict models `spike.floor`, `is_spike`'s two branches and beta's install threshold. It does NOT model nightly's 21-day build window, the `ndays=3` untestable prefix, `mature_after_days=5`/`mature_installs=4`, or `min_build_installs`. Every one of those makes selection harder, so P_strict is a LOWER bound on 'could never have selected'.

A 90-day total >= floor does NOT prove a build-day reached the floor, so the 90-day-report bar (18/350) is sufficient-not-necessary and I replaced it with the build-day measurement rather than quoting it as the answer.

The venue chain is unauthenticated by design, so a security-restricted bug is ABSENT, not an error: 'no open bug' could be wrong for a sec-restricted bug. None of the 44 is a poison-address signature, but the hole is real.

`_row_is_about` matches `cf_crash_signature` by case-insensitive SUBSTRING, so a bug about `LdrLoadDll | x` counts as a venue for `LdrLoadDll`. That biases the un-bugged rate DOWN — 78.4% is conservative.

The top-N-by-installs denominator is a PANEL, not the population a gate sees; ~60-70% of its 4-day churn is rank-boundary movement, not floor crossing. That is why I also report the rank-free >=K-installs slices.

This says nothing about whether any of these crashes is a real, fixable defect, and nothing about a regressor: these signatures predate every candidate window, so `regressed_by` is meaningless and no LLM run was made.
ESR is not measured here at all, and it is 39.4% of Firefox crash reports. A 'release-only' label is release-vs-nightly-vs-beta only.

(2) "The >=40/day tripwire FIRES" is not established: 7 burst run-days is a Poisson count whose exact 95% CI is [2.81, 14.42], putting the long-run rate at 33.6-85.5 UUIDs/day — straddling 40 — and the verdict is additionally conditional on NOT applying the burst fix the plan itself measured in §11 (ratio 3->5, 329->117 pairs). (3) Q2's advertised decision number, 29/37 = 78.4%, sits on the denominator the same report refutes two paragraphs earlier, and its topcrash control is volume-confounded to the point of tautology (test median 153 release installs, control median 4,317, zero overlap, 28x apart; topcrash keywords are assigned by volume).

The deploy-health report is the strongest of the three. I re-verified it at +60 min (three ingest ticks, 3 decline rows through TWO distinct skip paths, 3 running dossiers at 12:07Z, 0 5xx/H12/R14), and its log window genuinely covers a full post-deploy update_all, so its CONFIRMED / NOT-OBSERVABLE split is right. Net: the instrument disagreement on cost IS closed; the cost BAND is still open for three named reasons (window regime, burst-count sampling, and release's own $/dossier + useless rate) — none of which is the union factor any more.
